items.claim: `ClientMessage['t']` is partitioned into input vs authoring by four independent hand-written lists. ENGINE_INPUTS (client-message.ts:21) holds six tags; monitorInput (main.ts:375-417) switches over eight, adding `fireGraph`; voice-input.ts:117-122 lists six again with different membership; client-message.ts:507 tests just `midi|osc` for latency stamping. None is derived from another, so a new input message must be added in four places and a miss is silent — the message ends up unmonitored, unstamped, or accidentally editor-gated. The fireGraph divergence is the live symptom: main.ts monitors it as an input while ENGINE_INPUTS omits it, so requiresEditor('fireGraph') is true.

evidence.detail: apps/server/src/handlers/client-message.ts:21-28 — `const ENGINE_INPUTS: ReadonlySet<ClientMessage['t']> = new Set(['midi','osc','cc','programChange','key','recallSection']);` (no fireGraph).
apps/server/src/main.ts:411-414 — `case 'fireGraph': monitor({ type: 'graph', direction: 'in', … })` alongside the midi/cc/programChange/osc/key arms; the switch has no default.

apps/server/src/handlers/client-message.ts:55-57 — `requiresEditor(t) { return !ENGINE_INPUTS.has(t) && !UNGATED_NON_INPUTS.has(t); }`; the comment at :49-54 documents the deny-by-default intent, so the omission is security-relevant.
apps/server/src/handlers/voice-input.ts:117-122 lists setShow|key|fireGraph|recallSection|cc|programChange — a fourth, differently-shaped membership test.

items.proposed_fix: Declare ONE `Record<ClientMessage['t'], 'engine-input'|'authoring'|'read'|'voice-only'>` (apps/server/src/handlers/message-taxonomy.ts) so TypeScript demands a role per tag, and derive ENGINE_INPUTS, the voice-only test and the monitor label table from it. Encode fireGraph's CURRENT role ('authoring') so behaviour is preserved; raise the gating question separately rather than folding it into the mechanical unification.

removes_failure_path.justification: ENGINE_INPUTS feeds requiresEditor, the deny-by-default editor gate. A naive unification that adds fireGraph to the input set would let a viewer fire graphs, so any fix here touches a security guard and must not be auto-applied.

items.claim: One file maps NodeKind four times. kindIcon (:32), tint (:63) and kindLabel (:87) are `Record<NodeKind, …>` and therefore compiler-enforced; kindSummary (:118) is a switch ending in `default: return ''` at :156-157. A new kind is forced into the three Records but silently drops out of the fourth, shipping a node card with an icon, a tint and a title but a blank sub line. The fourth map is the only one that can go stale and the only one written as a defaulted switch.

evidence.detail: apps/web/src/lib/app/views/trigger-node-meta.ts:32 `export const kindIcon: Record<NodeKind, Component> = {…}` — 20 keys, enforced.

tsconfig.base.json sets `strict: true` and `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch: true` but NOT `noImplicitReturns`; a defaulted switch therefore carries no exhaustiveness obligation while a Record<NodeKind,…> does.

items.claim: The 13 ServerMessage variants declared once in packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts:390 are mirrored by 13 `on<X>?` fields in WSCallbacks (client.ts:39-82) and 13 arms in `private dispatch(msg: ServerMessage): void` (client.ts:244-285). Because dispatch returns void and has no default, omitting an arm is not a type error — a new server message decodes successfully and is then discarded with no log and no error.

evidence.detail: apps/web/src/lib/ws/client.ts:244-285 — `switch (msg.t)` over state/stats/input/monitor/projects/backups/presence/showLibrary/songLibrary/controllerDiscovery/controllerStatus/networkAdapters/error, no default and no exhaustiveness assertion.
packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts:390 serverMessageSchema is a z.discriminatedUnion with exactly 13 `t: z.literal(...)` members — currently in sync with the 13 dispatch arms.
apps/web/src/lib/ws/client.ts:39-82 — WSCallbacks declares one optional callback per variant; `this.cb.onX?.(…)` means a missing callback is also silent, compounding the drop.

items.proposed_fix: Add `default: { const _never: never = msg; void _never; break; }` to dispatch so the compiler rejects an unhandled ServerMessage variant. Optionally reshape WSCallbacks as `Partial<{ [K in ServerMessage['t']]: (msg: Extract<ServerMessage,{t:K}>) => void }>` so the callback surface is generated from the union rather than restated.

removes_failure_path.justification: Adding a never-check default arm adds a compile-time obligation; it removes no runtime guard, retry, timeout, fallback or validation.

items.claim: The Phase 1 lead is half right. render-plan.ts:49 nodeCategory IS compiler-enforced (no default, non-undefined declared return type under `strict`), so plan categorisation cannot silently miss a kind. The traversal switch at eval-graph.ts:389 sits in a void while-loop with no default and no never-assertion, so it is NOT enforced: a new NodeKind gets a plan category but no traversal arm and becomes an invisible dead end — a route that reaches it produces no light and raises no issue. The two must be edited in lockstep and only one of them tells you.

evidence.detail: packages/core/src/voice/eval-graph.ts:389 `switch (node.kind) {` … final arm at :582-588 `case 'randomMod': case 'envelope': case 'lfo': case 'cc': case 'note': case 'osc': break;` then `}` at :589 — no default, no exhaustiveness assertion.

packages/core/src/voice/render-plan.ts:49-78 `export function nodeCategory(kind: NodeKind): RenderPlanNodeCategory { switch (kind) { … } }` — every NodeKind covered, no default; under strictNullChecks a missing arm is TS2366.

tsconfig.base.json sets strict:true (hence strictNullChecks) and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch:true, but no noImplicitReturns — confirming the asymmetry: value-returning switches are enforced, void ones are not.

items.proposed_fix: Add `default: { const _never: never = node.kind; void _never; break; }` to the eval-graph.ts:389 switch. The compiler then flags the traversal site whenever nodeCategory must change, restoring lockstep at zero runtime cost. Deliberately-inert kinds keep their explicit no-op arms at :582-588, which documents the intent.

removes_failure_path.justification: A never-typed default is a compile-time assertion only; it removes no runtime guard, retry, timeout, fallback or validation and cannot alter eval behaviour for any existing kind.
